Alright, let me think about this year's plan. I'm 51, been farming my 40 mu for six years now — took it up when I came back from doing odd jobs. Never went to school, so I mostly watch what the others in the village do and remember what worked on my own ground.

## My thinking

I do wheat and maize, one after the other, same as most everyone around here. That's just how it's done — you harvest the wheat in June, and you got maybe a week to get the maize in the ground before it's too late. No time to waste.

**Wheat.** I plant it right after the National Day holiday, early October. I buy seed from the agro shop in town — an improved kind the shop owner sells, everybody around here uses it. Don't know the name exactly, but it's a good one. I use one bag of compound fertilizer (复合肥, the 15-15-15 kind) per mu before I sow — that's what my neighbor Old Wang does and his wheat looks good. Then in the spring when the ground softens and I water it the first time, I spread urea, about half a bag per mu. If the wheat looks a little yellow later on, maybe I add a bit more.

For water — the well costs money to pump, electricity ain't cheap. I give the wheat a winter watering before the freeze, then one at green-up in spring, then one when it's heading out. Three times usually. If it rains a lot I skip one.

I spray weeds once in spring, and if I see bugs or the leaves look funny I spray again. I don't like spraying too much, costs money.

Last year I got about 420 kg per mu on the wheat. Year before was better, maybe 450. I'm hoping for around 420-440 this year.

**Maize.** Right after the wheat combine comes through, I got to move fast. I pay the fellow with the no-till planter to come do my 40 mu — planting straight into the wheat stubble. Seed is a hybrid, I buy it fresh every year, you can't save maize seed. One bag per 4-5 mu roughly.

Same as wheat, I put one bag of compound at planting time — the planter drops it with the seed. Then when the maize is knee-high I spread urea around it, about half a bag per mu. That's usually enough.

Maize don't need as much water if the rain comes in July-August like it should. Maybe I irrigate once if it's dry at tasseling. Otherwise I save the pump money.

Spray for weeds once after planting. Armyworm if I see it.

I usually get around 470-500 kg per mu on the maize. Hoping for the same.

**Labor.** It's just me and my wife really working the land — our son works in the city. We do the walking-around work ourselves: fertilizing, checking the fields, spraying. For plowing, planting, and harvest I pay the machine guys. Can't do 40 mu by hand, not at my age.

**Money.** Seed, fertilizer, the machine people, the electric for the well, pesticide — all together I'll spend maybe 35,000-40,000 yuan this year for both crops. I keep some cash aside in case something goes wrong — a breakdown, a sick relative, whatever. You don't spend your last yuan on fertilizer.
